_provenance.decision_rule: WITHIN iff computing f on inputs <=20 uses only Tier A op KINDS (1-2 digit add/sub, mult <= 2dx1d/times tables, comparison/ordering, parity, small modulus, counting) for the bulk of the input domain. Anything requiring binary/digit decomposition, multi-digit multiplication or division as the CORE op, factorization, or checksum structure is BEYOND. Borderlines flagged and decided at freeze time; under-teach governs the CURRICULUM (S1 teaches only strict Tier A), not this grading list.

borderline_register.tension: n<=12 is strict times table; 13..20 needs 2dx2d which Tier A excludes (~38% of the 0..20 domain). Kept WITHIN: single application of the defining Tier A op kind; expect the untaught tail to cap its per-pair correctness and report it per-cell, not silently.

search/iteration flavour (like the prereg's gcd example), but verification is squares <=25 + comparison, all times-table. A B11 zero cell that is Tier-A-reducible — the sharpest rescue candidate the bottleneck thesis has.
op kind is Tier A (square + add) but composition needs two squares incl. the 2dx2d tail AND 3-digit addition (100+100 already at x=y=10); majority of the 0..20x0..20 domain exceeds tier. Kept BEYOND.
(x/step)*step = x - x%step; small modulus is Tier A and the reconstruction multiply has product <= x <= 20 (times table). Division-by-step is implicit in small modulus.

between_exclusive.why: two comparisons + conjunction; pure Tier A

is_lt_i16.why: comparison; 0..20 inputs are positive in i16 view so no reinterpretation burden

snap_down.why: x - x%step: small modulus + times-table reconstruction (product <= x <= 20); borderline, see register

isqrt.why: n<=20 -> result <=4; verify k*k<=n<(k+1)^2 with squares <=25 (times table) + comparison; borderline, see register

square.why: single small multiplication; 13..20 tail exceeds strict tier, see register

swap_bytes.why: byte manipulation (excluded class); on 0..20 equals x*256 — multi-digit multiplication

mask_overlap_count.why: bitwise + popcount; counting is Tier A but over binary decomposition, which is not

permille_to_byte.why: multi-digit multiplication + division as the core op

luhn_check.why: checksum / digit manipulation — explicitly excluded in §3.1

geom_circle_circumference_approx.why: multi-digit multiplication by a 4-digit constant + shift

pow_small.why: repeated multi-digit multiplication with saturation logic; kin of the excluded modular exponentiation

permille.why: multi-digit multiplication + division as the core op

norm2_sq.why: two squares incl. 2dx2d tail + 3-digit addition; borderline, see register
